blocks.content: Beaches are characteristic features of shorelines dominated by deposition, built up by constructive waves.

rows: Attached to land at one end
Longshore drift carrying sand across a bay entrance
Wave refraction depositing sediment in the lee of an island
Wave action breaking offshore and depositing sand ridges

items: Constructive waves have a stronger swash than backwash, leading to net sediment deposition on the shore.
Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest coastal lagoon in India, formed by depositional barrier spits.
Longshore drift (littoral drift) is the primary transport mechanism responsible for spit and bar formation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Depositional coastal landforms primarily form along low-energy coasts dominated by constructive wave action.
Beaches represent temporary or permanent accumulations of sand, pebbles, or cobbles along the shoreline.
Spits are elongated depositional ridges attached to the mainland at one end and projecting into open water.
Tombolos are specialized sand bars that join an offshore island to the mainland or another island.
Lagoons are coastal bodies of water separated from the ocean by barrier islands, spits, or offshore bars.
